english.title: Driver / operator / manager fail to stop smoking in smoke-free vehicle used for private purpose child present - Wales
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being

(A)_[the driver]_
(B)_[the operator]_
(C)_[a person concerned in the management]_

of a vehicle which was not within regulation 15(2) of the Smoke-free Premises and Vehicles (Wales) Regulations 2020 and was used for social, domestic or other private purposes and more than one person was present in the vehicle and one of those persons was a child, namely **(..SPECIFY CHILD..), failed to take reasonable steps to cause a person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON SMOKING..), smoking in that vehicle to stop smoking
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 15(1) and (3)(b) and 17 of the Smoke-free Premises and Vehicles (Wales) Regulations 2020 and sections 6(5)(c), (6) and (9) and 15 of the Public Health (Wales) Act 2017.

english.notes:
(i) A child is a person under 18, see section 28 of the Public Health (Wales) Act 2017.
(ii) Smoke-free vehicles are defined in regulation 15 of the Smoke-free Premises and Vehicles (Wales) Regulations 2020. Vehicles which are smoke-free by virtue of paragraph (3) are smoke-free only when the vehicle is being used as described in that paragraph.
(iii) Where the vehicle is used wholly or mainly in the course of paid or voluntary work and by more than one person or to transport members of the public, see H22454/PH17011. Where the vehicle is not used in such way but person present for the purpose of receiving goods or services, see H22455/PH17012.
(iv) For a defence where the person did not know, and could not reasonably have been expected to know, that the person in question was smoking, see section 6(7) and (8) of the Public Health (Wales) Act 2017.
(v) The fixed penalty amount is £100 (regulation 20(c)); the discounted amount £75 (regulation 21(c)). For the form of the fixed penalty notice, see regulation 22.
(vi) The enforcement authority in relation to vehicles in its area which are smoke-free under regulation 15(3)(b) is the chief officer of police for the police area, see regulation 19; this is in addition to local authorities which are enforcement authorities under section 18 of the Public Health (Wales) Act 2017.
